caption: NSFAS covers the big stuff. Nobody warns you about the printing. What's the cost that caught you out first year?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R9 200
p/m income
Living in Potchefstroom
slides.body:
Female, 21
Single, university student
NSFAS allowance + part-time retail job
Net income: R9 200 p/m

slides.title: Res top-up
slides.includes: NSFAS covers most of it, this is what's left to pay myself
slides.body: The allowance is generous. It still doesn't cover all of it.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Res kitchen, mostly instant meals and Sunday cooking
slides.body: I eat well exactly one day a week, and it's not by accident.

slides.title: Data & wifi
slides.includes: Online modules, group project calls, the res wifi that drops during load shedding
slides.body: Non-negotiable. My degree runs on data more than it runs on textbooks.

slides.title: Textbooks & printing
slides.includes: Secondhand textbooks, printing readings I forget to budget for
slides.body: I've never once budgeted enough for printing. Every single semester.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Home for holidays, the odd trip into town for groceries
slides.body: Campus is walkable. Home for the holidays isn't.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Toiletries, the odd meal deal, a small amount home to my younger sister, a stokvel with my res friends, my mom's insistence on a funeral policy
slides.body: Small things, but there are a lot of them for a student income.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R9 200. That's tight, but it's mine, and I've never once run out before month end.

slides.title: I stopped losing track between allowance drops
slides.body:
I upload my statement to Beyond Horizon the day the NSFAS allowance lands.

The printing costs were the thing I never once accounted for until I could actually see them.

No bank login needed.
